o1.biggest_strength: On-brand, grade-8 launch copy with real angles — a five-post X thread, a "start with five" first-day path for the newcomer persona, named author credits, and per-video growth math (about 750 kept per video, 6,750 across nine creators).
o1.biggest_mistake: The channel table is headed and framed as "users who stay" but puts extension authors (2,470) at #2 above X (3,740), Hacker News (2,940) and Product Hunt (3,420) without stating the growth basis, so the ranking looks like an arithmetic error; the copy also ships with blanks ([Opens in __ ms on a __ Mac], [Extension] by [author], [support address]) and there is no owner column or contingency plan.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: State plainly that the rank is by retention rate and growth headroom, and finish every piece of copy with no blanks plus an owner on each timeline row.

o2.biggest_strength: Turns the migration history into an operating plan: existing users go out in three gated waves (42,000/168,000/210,000, summing to the 420,000 list), Product Hunt and Hacker News move to 15 December, and new users can still launch on 8 December because "new users have no settings to lose" — with a no-go rule and day-4 plan B, all numbers traceable (93,500 installs, 17,080 kept, 18%, 19% of installs/41% of retained).
o2.biggest_mistake: It breaks the brand rule to always credit extension authors by name — neither the X post nor the email names a single author (only a general "built by someone in our community") — and "kept the lowest share" overstates the case, since Hacker News at 14% was fourth of five, not the lowest.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Name three extension authors in the launch post and email, and fix the Product Hunt/Hacker News retention claim.

reason: Both get the retention math and the migration gate right, but Output 2 gives me a plan I can run tomorrow: a decision block, owners on every row, three gated waves that sum to my list, a no-go rule and a plan B, while Output 1 leaves blanks in the copy and headlines a ranking its own numbers contradict.
